title: SDK route tagging guidance (draft) — Python / TypeScript / Go
body:
Last updated: 2026-02-20
Owner: Monica Patel (DevEx)
Status: DRAFT — pending final API naming alignment across SDKs + gateway behavior confirmation.

Purpose
This doc explains how to attach a stable "route" identifier to Redwood Inference requests so the Console can attribute cost + latency by route and by model.

If you tag routes consistently:
- Console → Usage Insights will show Top cost drivers grouped by route.
- Route Detail view will break down spend + latency by model variant (including fallback routing events).
- Exports (CSV/JSON) can be used for FinOps/chargeback and incident cost reviews.

This guidance applies to:
- Hosted API
- Dedicated
- Private (VPC/on-prem) — same route semantics; note data residency/retention policies still apply.

What is a “route”?
A route is a developer-supplied identifier representing the logical endpoint/feature in your product that initiated the LLM call.
Examples:
- "chat/support_agent"
- "summarize/ticket"
- "search/rerank"
- "onboarding/email_draft"

Route is NOT a URL path from your public API (though you can reuse those conventions if they are stable).

High-level behavior
- If you provide a route explicitly via SDK option or header, Redwood uses it.
- If you do not provide a route, Redwood may derive one in the gateway (if enabled) or will record "unknown" / "unattributed" depending on deployment.
- Route is normalized and may be truncated; invalid characters may be replaced. If your route exceeds limits or violates guardrails, it may be bucketed/hashed (see Cardinality + limits).

Naming conventions (strongly recommended)
Goal: stable, low-cardinality identifiers that align with how your org wants to allocate cost.

Do:
- Use a small, human-readable namespace.
  - Format: "<domain>/<feature>[/<action>]"
  - Example: "support/chat" and "support/chat:tool_calls" (if you need one more level)
- Keep the set of unique routes bounded.
  - Think: 10–500 routes per project/environment, not unbounded.
- Use lowercase and consistent separators.
- Keep route values stable over time; treat them like metrics dimensions.

Don’t:
- Do not include user IDs, account IDs, ticket IDs, emails, or any PII.
  - BAD: "support/chat/user_934857"
  - BAD: "summarize/ticket/INC-102938"
- Do not embed timestamps, random IDs, request IDs.
  - BAD: "chat/1708041123"
- Do not include full URLs with querystrings.
  - BAD: "/v1/chat?org=abc&user=123"

Recommended mapping strategy
- Use your application’s internal routing/handler name (controller/action) or feature flag name.
- If you have multiple deployments/environments, keep route values identical across envs; environment is a separate filter in Console (prod/staging/dev).

Cardinality + limits (important)
(Confirming final numbers with Telemetry; keep this section in sync with Confluence “cost attribution cardinality guardrails”)
- Route length: keep under ~120 characters.
- Allowed characters: alphanumeric plus: / _ - : .
- Any value outside guardrails may be normalized, truncated, or bucketed.
- If you exceed cardinality budgets, you may see:
  - “Other”/bucketed routes
  - “Unknown route” dominating top drivers
  - degraded freshness for insights (aggregation pressure)

If you think you need high-cardinality routing (e.g., per-tenant chargeback): do NOT encode tenant in route. Use org/project scoping and/or separate projects, and talk to Redwood if you need additional dimensions (out of scope for initial GA).

How to set route in SDKs
Note: exact API names depend on SDK versions. The intent is consistent across SDKs:
- Per-request route: override for a single call.
- Default route: set on the client for an entire service or module.

Python (redwood-sdk-python)
Version note: route tagging support is being added/standardized in PR #417.

Option A — per-request route (recommended)

from redwood import Redwood

client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this ticket..."}],
    route="support/summarize_ticket",
)

Option B — set a default route at client construction

client = Redwood(
    api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"],
    default_route="support/service",
)

# Later overrides are still allowed:
resp = client.embeddings.create(
    model="redwood/text-embedding-3-large",
    input=["..."],
    route="support/search_index",
)

Streaming
Route should be attached at request start; it must be set before streaming begins.

with client.chat.completions.stream(
    model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Draft a reply..."}],
    route="support/draft_reply",
) as stream:
    for event in stream:
        ...

TypeScript (redwood-sdk-typescript)
Version note: route tagging support is being added/standardized in PR #233.

Option A — per-request route

import { Redwood } from "@redwood-ai/sdk";

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY! });

const out = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Help me respond to this customer..." }],
  route: "support/draft_reply",
});

Option B — client default route

const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY!,
  defaultRoute: "support/service",
});

await client.rerank.create({
  model: "redwood/rerank-v2",
  query: "refund policy",
  documents: docs,
  route: "support/kb_rerank",
});

Express / Next.js middleware pattern
If you have many call-sites, wrap the client and pass route from the handler name.

export async function handleTicketSummarize(req, res) {
  const route = "support/summarize_ticket";
  const result = await client.chat.completions.create({
    model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: req.body.text }],
    route,
  });
  res.json(result);
}

Go (redwood-sdk-go)
Status note: route tagging API shape is still being finalized for Go; this is the intended pattern.

Option A — per-request option

client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithAPIKey(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")))

resp, err := client.ChatCompletions.Create(ctx, &redwood.ChatCompletionsRequest{
  Model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  Messages: []redwood.Message{{Role: "user", Content: "Summarize..."}},
  Route: "support/summarize_ticket",
})

Option B — context-based route (if/when supported)

ctx := redwood.WithRoute(context.Background(), "support/draft_reply")
resp, err := client.ChatCompletions.Create(ctx, req)

Gin example (deriving from handler)

func DraftReplyHandler(c *gin.Context) {
  route := "support/draft_reply"
  // set route explicitly when calling Redwood
  resp, err := rw.ChatCompletions.Create(c.Request.Context(), &redwood.ChatCompletionsRequest{...
    Route: route,
  })
  ...
}

Gateway / proxy integration (header-based)
If you call Redwood through a service mesh, gateway, or custom HTTP client (not via SDK), set the route header.

Header name
- Draft proposal: "X-Redwood-Route: <route>"
- Alternative names discussed: "Redwood-Route" or "X-Route" (do not implement alternatives until ADR final).

Example (raw HTTP)
POST /v1/chat/completions
X-Redwood-Route: support/draft_reply
Authorization: Bearer ...

{
  "model": "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  "messages": [...]
}

If you already have OpenTelemetry
Do not assume OTel span.name automatically becomes Redwood route. For now, route must be set via SDK or header. (We may add optional mapping later; out of scope for GA.)

Common framework patterns
FastAPI (Python)
Use a dependency or helper that sets route based on your endpoint function.

from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/draft_reply")
def draft_reply(payload: Payload):
    route = "support/draft_reply"
    return client.chat.completions.create(
        model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": payload.text}],
        route=route,
    )

Django (Python)
Use a module-level constant per view or a decorator.

ROUTE = "support/summarize_ticket"

def summarize_ticket(request):
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(..., route=ROUTE)
    ...

Next.js (TypeScript)
In route handlers (app/api/*), set route explicitly.

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const route = "support/draft_reply";
  const body = await req.json();
  const out = await client.chat.completions.create({
    model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: body.text }],
    route,
  });
  return Response.json(out);
}

Troubleshooting

1) Console shows “Unknown route” for most spend
Likely causes:
- You never set route in SDK/header.
- Route is being dropped in a proxy layer.
- You’re setting route only in some code paths (e.g., non-streaming but not streaming).

Checklist:
- Confirm SDK version supports route tagging.
- Inspect one request (server logs / gateway logs) for presence of the route field/header.
- Verify you are not overriding route with an empty string.

2) Route list is full of near-duplicates (cardinality explosion)
Likely causes:
- You embedded IDs (tenant, user, ticket) in route.
- You used a URL path with dynamic segments.

Fix:
- Replace dynamic segments with a constant token.
  - BAD: "support/ticket/INC-18420/summarize"
  - GOOD: "support/ticket/summarize"

3) I set route but it doesn’t appear immediately
Usage Insights are near-real-time but not instantaneous. Expect some delay due to aggregation and late-arriving metering.

4) Invoice vs Console route totals don’t match
Console “usage insights” are built from telemetry aggregates and may differ slightly from invoicing totals depending on cutoffs, late data, retention windows, and rounding. Use Console exports for route attribution and invoices for billing totals.

Open questions / TODOs (for finalization)
- Confirm final header name and exact normalization rules from ADR.
- Confirm SDK option names (route vs requestRoute; default_route vs defaultRoute) and document version gating.
- Add a short section on model fallback attribution semantics (route stays constant; model dimension may vary within same route).
- Add a minimal snippet to quickstarts (coordinate with redwood-quickstarts PR #109).

Notes to self (Monica)
- Keep examples consistent with Console IA wording: “Routes”, “Top cost drivers”, “Export report”.
- Ensure we never imply route is user-provided freeform; emphasize guardrails.
- Add link to docs FAQ about Unknown route and cardinality budgets once Elliot/Wei publish final docs page.
